findings.location: ExactToken.pull(address,address,uint256) (src/libraries/ExactToken.sol#11-18) uses arbitrary from in transferFrom: IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(from,address(this),amount) (src/libraries/ExactToken.sol#15)
findings.rationale: ExactToken.pull is internal. Every production caller supplies its authenticated msg.sender (owner for activate/increase; bound Vault/Fees/Receiver/router/authenticated provider for module transfers). There is no externally selectable victim address. Both sender and recipient deltas are checked; module/token trust remains a deployment gate.

mint/increase/swap public entries are nonReentrant and restricted to fixed custody/buyback modules. Private helpers are only reached under those guards. The intentionally callable unlockCallback requires the fixed PoolManager plus the pending payload hash and consumes the hash before settlement. Exact transfers, LP ownership, liquidity deltas and approval resets are enforced. This conclusion assumes the reviewed fixed Uniswap/token dependencies; pinned fork tests cover ordinary settlement.

execute is onlyKeeper/live/nonReentrant. Vault principal release and bridge send are separately module-restricted and guarded; exact token deltas and zeroed allowances are checked. The immutable production transport must be independently reviewed: a valid code interface or balance delta does not prove remote asset delivery.

findings.location: ZZZFeeController.allocate(uint256,address,uint256) (src/ZZZFeeController.sol#48-76) performs a multiplication on the result of a division:
findings.rationale: Intentional 5/3/1/1 ten-raw-unit batch allocation. total % 10 is carried in dust, not lost or credited twice. Multiplying total first would change the rounding policy and can overflow. Unit/fuzz and independent integer-ledger stateful invariants check conservation; small fees may remain pending until a batch or explicit flush.

findings.location: ZZZStrategy._floor(int24,int24) (src/ZZZStrategy.sol#13-17) performs a multiplication on the result of a division:
findings.rationale: Strategy._floor deliberately divides signed ticks, adjusts negative nonmultiples, then multiplies by spacing to return the aligned floor. This is integer tick alignment, not an accidental loss of price precision; signed-boundary strategy regressions cover it.

findings.location: BridgeAssets.assets(Route,BridgeMessage,bool).count (src/libraries/BridgeAssets.sol#12) is a local variable never initialized
findings.rationale: Solidity initializes the local memory struct/integer to zero. Bridge ACK count intentionally remains zero; the Principal/Reward branches set it. Receiver origin explicitly assigns all imported identity/contribution fields and importPending constructs local state. Fee bridge message explicitly assigns the required Reward fields, while ACK/principal-only fields intentionally remain zero; typed receiver checks enforce message kind.

findings.location: ZZZBridgeRouter._settled(address[],uint256[],address) (src/ZZZBridgeRouter.sol#105-110) has external calls inside a loop: IERC20(tokens[i]).balanceOf(address(this)) != beforeBalances[i] (src/ZZZBridgeRouter.sol#108)
findings.rationale: Loops are explicitly bounded: bridge messages have 0 ACK, 1 Reward, or 2 Principal assets; Rewards.checkpointAll has at most MAX_ASSETS=32. Reads use fixed module/view getters and admitted tokens. The 32-funded-asset cold benchmark measures ~2.50M execution gas; this is bounded but costly and token blacklisting can halt an operation. Live network budgeting remains required.

Private _principal is reached from nonReentrant receiveMessage, restricted to the fixed Bridge. Receipt/provenance changes roll back if any later transfer/import fails. registerImport is fixed-module authorized, tokens are exact-delta checked, and the fixed Vault import entry is separately guarded. Provider and destination trust are not removed by these guards.

The named private helper is reachable only through Vault nonReentrant custody entry points, or the named public entry itself has that guard and its live/module/owner check. No external dependency can reenter a mutable Vault path through these helpers. _idle updates enforce aggregate backing, LP spending/ownership is checked, and fee transfers preserve separate ledgers. Malicious approved token/governance behavior can still deny service or change economic assumptions; no unconditional security claim is made.

findings.location: ZZZMigrationRegistry.add(Route,bytes32) (src/ZZZMigrationRegistry.sol#18-56) has a high cyclomatic complexity (14).
findings.rationale: Route onboarding has many deliberate chain/module/token/decimal/kind checks. Removing checks to reduce this metric would weaken custody. Unit migration and route tests exercise invalid configurations; provider, future destination and full cross-chain stateful review remain open.

mintDormant forwards exactly the paid 0.05 ETH to the immutable recipient under nonReentrant, reverting NFT issuance/proceeds atomically on failure. Paid-mint tests cover recipient and NFT receiver reentrancy/rejection. A recipient that permanently rejects ETH can permanently prevent minting; select/test the immutable recipient before deployment.

Structural interface suggestion. Minimal external interfaces intentionally coexist with concrete module ABIs; compiler/ABI tests and typed adapter tests validate selected signatures. In particular MigrationRegistry.get(bytes32) returns Route and is not semantically IZZZPools.get(bytes32), despite the equal input selector. This finding does not justify inheriting the suggested unrelated interface.
